target: mandark -- Dell XPS 13 7390, rebuilt for boot speed
goal: power-on to a login shell, minimum wall clock
notes: Facts only. Status is NOT stored here -- verify.py derives it. A fact with no probe can never rise above 'researched'; writing one is a promise to find a probe or delete it.

facts.claim: The machine is a Dell XPS 13 7390 (non-2-in-1).
Root is a plain NVMe partition with no LVM layer, so the clone needs only growpart+resize2fs.
The BT/WLAN combo card is soldered; it cannot be swapped during the rebuild. A USB dongle is the accepted fix.
There is no coreboot port for the XPS 13 7390, so Dell UEFI POST time is a floor we cannot remove.
Firmware POST completes in under 8s.
After BIOS tuning (Fastboot=Minimal, UEFI network stack off, unused controllers off) POST completes in under 4s.
facts.source: prose estimate, 2026-08-15 -- 2-3s claimed saving is unmeasured

facts.claim: Secure Boot is disabled, so a self-built EFI-stub kernel boots without signing.
Power-on to terminal takes 1 second.
facts.probe: systemd-analyze time | sed -n '1s/.*= //p' | awk '{t=0; for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){if($i~/min/){sub(/min/,"",$i); t+=$i*60} else if($i~/s$/){sub(/s$/,"",$i); t+=$i}}; print t}'

facts.claim: Everything we control -- loader, kernel, userspace -- totals under 1.5s.
facts.probe: systemd-analyze time | grep -oE '[0-9.]+s \((loader|kernel|userspace)\)' | grep -oE '^[0-9.]+' | paste -sd+ | bc

facts.claim: systemd-boot, not GRUB, is the installed bootloader.
The bootloader menu timeout is 0, so no wall-clock is spent waiting for a keypress.
nvme, the root filesystem driver and i915 are compiled into the kernel, so no initramfs is unpacked at boot.
facts.source: prose recommendation, 2026-08-15 -- largest kernel-side win, not yet attempted

facts.claim: The default systemd target is multi-user, not graphical -- 'terminal' is the goal, and a display manager costs 1-3s.
getty@tty1 autologins, so power-on lands on a shell with no password prompt in the path.
No *-wait-online unit is enabled. These block boot for pure dead time.
snapd is not installed. It costs seeding time at boot and mount units forever after.
plymouth is absent, so nothing waits on a splash screen to quit.
No single userspace unit costs more than 500ms.
facts.probe: systemd-analyze blame --no-pager | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+ms|[0-9.]+s' | head -1 | awk '/ms/{gsub(/ms/,"");print} /s/{gsub(/s/,"");print $1*1000}'

facts.claim: fstrim.timer is active, so the NVMe does not degrade into slow writes after the rebuild.
Every fstab entry is UUID-keyed, so the clone from external enclosure to internal disk boots without edits.
A 10Gbps USB-C NVMe enclosure (JMS583 or ASM2364) plus a spare NVMe is the build medium, so the trial install runs on the identical hardware and drivers as the final one.
facts.source: prose recommendation, 2026-08-15 -- hardware not yet acquired

facts.claim: Transfer is dd of the whole device, then `sgdisk -e` to relocate the GPT backup header, then growpart+resize2fs for the size difference.
facts.source: prose recommendation, 2026-08-15 -- procedure untested on this estate. CAVEAT: the growpart+resize2fs half assumes hw.root-disk-is-nvme, which the current machine refutes (root is /dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-ubuntu--lv). Under LVM the tail is pvresize + lvextend + resize2fs instead. The target build should drop LVM and make this moot.
